title: Community Shaping in the Digital Age: A Temporal Fusion Framework for Analyzing Discourse Fragmentation in Online Social Networks
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the presence and temporal dynamics of 'Religious Intolerance' as one of eight categories of harmful language/hate speech within online social networks (Twitter) during major U.S. events in 2020.
findings: Religious intolerance was identified as a fragment of online discrimination discourse, although it represented a smaller proportion of the hate speech analyzed compared to xenophobia and homophobia. Additionally, the study found that machine learning classification models occasionally made questionable classifications of religious intolerance due to spurious correlations within the training data.
